record.paper_title: Exploring Progressions: A Collection of Problems
record.original_question: Suppose a sequence (a_n) satisfies the recurrence a_{n+1} = (a_n + λ)ω, where λ and ω are fixed real numbers with ω ≠ 1. Prove by induction that for every natural number n, a_n = a_1 ω^(n−1) + λ((ω^n − ω)/(ω − 1)), and then use that formula to show that the partial sums satisfy S_n = a_1 + a_2 + ··· + a_n = a_1((ω^n − 1)/(ω − 1)) + λ((ω^(n+1) − nω^2 + (n−1)ω)/(ω−1)^2).

evidence.quote: Suppose that the sequence a1, a2, . . . , an, . . . satisfies an+1 = (an+λ)·ω, where λ and ω are fixed real numbers with ω 6= 1. (i) Use mathematical induction to prove that for every natural number, an = a1 · ω^(n−1) + λ · ((ω^n−ω)/(ω−1)). (ii) Use your answer in part (i) to show that, Sn = a1 + a2 + . . . + an = a1 · ((ω^n − 1)/(ω − 1)) + λ · ((ω^(n+1)−n·ω^2+(n−1)ω)/(ω−1)^2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda$ and $\omega$ be fixed real numbers with $\omega 
eq 1$, and let $(a_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of real numbers satisfying the recurrence
$$a_{n+1} = (a_n + \lambda)\,\omega \qquad 	ext{for all } n \geq 1.$$

(i) Prove by mathematical induction that for every natural number $n \geq 1$,
$$a_n = a_1\,\omega^{n-1} + \lambda\cdot rac{\omega^n - \omega}{\omega - 1}.$$

(ii) Using the formula in (i), prove that for every natural number $n \geq 1$, the partial sum $S_n = a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n$ is given by
$$S_n = a_1\cdot rac{\omega^n - 1}{\omega - 1} + \lambda\cdot rac{\omega^{n+1} - n\,\omega^2 + (n-1)\,\omega}{(\omega - 1)^2}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is a standard exercise on a first-order affine linear recurrence. The closed-form solution and its summation are obtained by direct induction (or by solving the affine recurrence via its fixed point), so the result is fully established by elementary means.

status_evidence.title: First-order linear recurrence (closed form)
status_evidence.snippet: A first-order linear recurrence a_{n+1}=c\,a_n+d has the explicit solution a_n=c^{n-1}a_1+d(c^{n-1}-1)/(c-1) when c\neq 1.
status_evidence.claim: The explicit formula in (i) is a standard consequence of solving an affine linear recurrence and its summation yields the formula in (ii).
